theory.intro: Changing how a loan is repaid changes both how long it runs and how much it costs. Paying more each period, paying more often, or paying a lump sum all cut the balance sooner, so less interest is charged.
facts: Interest is charged on the balance owing, so anything that lowers the balance sooner lowers the interest charged.
A larger repayment clears the loan in fewer periods, so the total repaid is smaller even though each payment is bigger.
Total repaid $=$ repayment $\times$ number of repayments, so two options are compared by working out each total.
Fortnightly repayments of half the monthly amount are made $26$ times a year, which is more than $12$ monthly payments.
A **lump-sum payment** is a single extra amount paid off the balance; it shortens the term while the regular repayment stays the same.
With a lump sum, the total paid is the regular repayments actually made plus the lump sum itself.
An extra payment saves more interest early in a loan, when the balance owing is at its largest.
steps: Work out the total repaid under the first option.
Work out the total repaid under the second option, adding any lump sum.
Subtract to find the saving, or subtract the amount borrowed to find the interest.

foundation.question_text: A loan of $\$5000$ is charged interest at $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Find the balance at the end of the first month if the repayment is $\$250$, and if it is $\$400$.
foundation.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.12}{12} = 0.01$
$I = 5000 \times 0.01 = \$50$

At $\$250$: balance $= 5000 + 50 - 250 = \$4800$
At $\$400$: balance $= 5000 + 50 - 400 = \$4650$

The larger repayment leaves $\$150$ less owing.

foundation.question_text: A loan of $\$180\,000$ can be repaid monthly at $\$1450$ over $20$ years, or fortnightly at $\$725$ over $17$ years. Which option costs less in total, and by how much?
foundation.solution_text:
Monthly: total $= 1450 \times 12 \times 20$
$= \$348\,000$

Fortnightly: total $= 725 \times 26 \times 17$
$= \$320\,450$

The fortnightly option costs less:
$348\,000 - 320\,450 = \$27\,550$ less

foundation.question_text: A borrower owes $\$84\,000$ on a loan charged at $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. She pays a lump sum of $\$15\,000$ off the balance. By how much does the next month's interest charge fall?
foundation.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.072}{12} = 0.006$

Before: $I = 84\,000 \times 0.006 = \$504$
After: $I = 69\,000 \times 0.006 = \$414$

The interest charge falls by $504 - 414 = \$90$.

foundation.question_text: Explain why repaying a loan fortnightly, rather than monthly with double the amount, reduces the total interest paid.
foundation.solution_text:
The balance is reduced every two weeks instead of every four, so interest is charged on a smaller balance for more of the time.
There are also $26$ fortnights but only $12$ months in a year, so slightly more is repaid each year.
Both effects clear the loan sooner, so less interest is charged.

foundation.question_text: A borrower decides to pay $\$50$ more each month than the required repayment on a reducing balance loan. Describe the effect on the term of the loan and on the total interest paid.
foundation.solution_text:
The extra $\$50$ comes straight off the balance, so the balance falls faster.
A smaller balance is charged less interest, so the loan is repaid in fewer months.
The term is shorter and the total interest paid is lower.

foundation.question_text: A loan of $\$9000$ is charged interest at $18\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Find the interest charged in the **second** month if the repayment is $\$500$, and if it is $\$700$.
foundation.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.18}{12} = 0.015$
$I = 9000 \times 0.015 = \$135$ in month $1$

At $\$500$: balance $= 9000 + 135 - 500 = \$8635$
Month $2$: $I = 8635 \times 0.015 = \$129.53$

At $\$700$: balance $= 9000 + 135 - 700 = \$8435$
Month $2$: $I = 8435 \times 0.015 = \$126.53$

The larger repayment saves $\$3.00$ of interest in the second month alone.

development.question_text: A loan of $\$320\,000$ can be repaid monthly at $\$2210$ over $30$ years, or fortnightly at $\$1105$ over $26$ years. Find the difference in the total interest paid under the two methods.

A loan of $\$280\,000$ is repaid at $\$1650$ per month over $25$ years. After $8$ years the borrower pays a lump sum of $\$50\,000$, and the loan is then fully repaid after a further $156$ monthly repayments. How much less is paid overall?
development.solution_text:
Without the lump sum: total $= 1650 \times 12 \times 25$
$= \$495\,000$

With the lump sum:
Number of repayments $= 8 \times 12 + 156 = 252$
Total $= 1650 \times 252 + 50\,000$
$= 415\,800 + 50\,000$
$= \$465\,800$

Difference $= 495\,000 - 465\,800$
$= \$29\,200$

development.question_text: A loan of $\$250\,000$ is due to be repaid at $\$1580$ per month over $25$ years. Instead the borrower pays $\$1700$ per month, clearing the loan in $254$ months. How much is saved in total?

development.solution_text:
At $\$800$ per month the curve reaches zero at about $140$ months.
Total $= 800 \times 140 = \$112\,000$

At $\$1200$ per month the curve reaches zero at about $70$ months.
Total $= 1200 \times 70 = \$84\,000$

Difference $= 112\,000 - 84\,000$
$= \$28\,000$ less

development.question_text: A loan of $\$200\,000$ is repaid at $\$1400$ per month over $30$ years. After $12$ years a lump sum of $\$40\,000$ is paid, and the loan is fully repaid after a further $132$ monthly repayments. Find the total saving.
development.solution_text:
Without the lump sum: total $= 1400 \times 12 \times 30$
$= \$504\,000$

With the lump sum:
Number of repayments $= 12 \times 12 + 132 = 276$
Total $= 1400 \times 276 + 40\,000$
$= 386\,400 + 40\,000$
$= \$426\,400$

Saving $= 504\,000 - 426\,400$
$= \$77\,600$

development.question_text: A personal loan of $\$12\,000$ is charged interest at $10.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly with repayments of $\$300$. The borrower instead pays an extra $\$50$ each month. Compare the balances owing at the end of the second month.

mastery.question_text: A loan of $\$400\,000$ is repaid at $\$2650$ per month over $30$ years. After $10$ years the borrower increases the repayment to $\$3200$ per month and the loan is repaid after a further $172$ months. How much less is paid in total?
mastery.solution_text:
Without the increase: total $= 2650 \times 12 \times 30$
$= \$954\,000$

With the increase:
First $10$ years: $2650 \times 120 = \$318\,000$
Remaining $172$ months: $3200 \times 172 = \$550\,400$
Total $= 318\,000 + 550\,400 = \$868\,400$

Difference $= 954\,000 - 868\,400$
$= \$85\,600$ less

mastery.question_text: A loan of $\$240\,000$ can be repaid monthly at $\$1718$ over $20$ years, or fortnightly at $\$859$ over $17$ years and $6$ months. Find the difference in the total interest paid.

A loan of $\$150\,000$ was to be repaid at $\$1250$ per month over $20$ years. After $5$ years a lump sum of $\$30\,000$ is paid, and the loan is cleared by a further $122$ monthly repayments. Find the total saving and the number of months by which the term is shortened.
mastery.solution_text:
Without the lump sum: total $= 1250 \times 12 \times 20$
$= \$300\,000$ over $240$ months

With the lump sum:
Number of repayments $= 5 \times 12 + 122 = 182$
Total $= 1250 \times 182 + 30\,000$
$= 227\,500 + 30\,000$
$= \$257\,500$

Saving $= 300\,000 - 257\,500 = \$42\,500$
Term shortened by $240 - 182 = 58$ months
